questions.q: When the mail team reached Skaguay at the start of the chapter, what was wrong with the dogs?
choices: They were sick from eating the frozen horse-hide
They were dead tired from months of hard toil
They had been hurt in a fight with the police dogs
They were half-frozen after falling through the ice
questions.evidence: There was nothing the matter with them except that they were dead tired.

questions.q: Why were Buck and his tired mates sold instead of given a long rest?
choices: Their driver wanted to go home and could not take them along
The Judge had sent a letter asking for Buck to be returned
Orders said fresh dogs would replace them and they would be sold
They had been caught stealing from the mail train's food sacks
questions.evidence: Fresh batches of Hudson Bay dogs were to take the places of those worthless for the trail.

questions.q: What did Hal's belt full of cartridges, a gun and a knife show about him?
choices: That he was a skilled hunter who had lived many years in the North
That he was very young and had no real experience at all
That he was a police officer sent to guard the mail
That he was planning to rob the miners in Dawson
questions.evidence: It advertised his callowness

questions.q: How were Hal, Charles and Mercedes related?
choices: Mercedes was Charles's wife and Hal's sister
Mercedes was Hal's wife and Charles's daughter
Hal and Charles were brothers, and Mercedes was their cousin
Charles was Hal's father, and Mercedes was Hal's aunt
questions.evidence: She was Charles's wife and Hal's sister

questions.q: When Buck first saw his new owners' camp, what did it tell him about them?
choices: That they were careless and messy in everything they did
That they were rich and had brought every comfort from home
That they had travelled the trail to Dawson many times before
That they had already bought a strong team of fresh dogs
questions.evidence: a slipshod and slovenly affair

questions.q: What advice did a man from a neighboring tent give about the tent?
choices: To buy a bigger one before leaving Skaguay
Not to take it along, since it was springtime
To pack it on the front of the sled, not the back
To sell it to the miners for extra dog food
questions.evidence: I wouldn't tote that tent along if I was you

questions.q: Why couldn't the dogs move the sled at first, even when Hal whipped them?
choices: The dogs were tied to a post that Hal had forgotten about
The sled's runners had frozen fast to the packed snow
The sled was stuck in a deep rut in the main street
Buck had told the team to refuse to pull for Hal
questions.evidence: The runners are froze fast.

questions.q: What happened as the top-heavy sled swung around the turn into the main street?
choices: It tipped over, spilling half its load, and the dogs ran on
It slid into a snowbank and the dogs stopped to rest
It hit a wagon, and Hal had to pay the owner for it
It broke in two, and Charles had to build a new one
questions.evidence: As they swung on the turn the sled went over

questions.q: What advice did the people of Skaguay give after the sled tipped over?
choices: Wait for summer and travel to Dawson by riverboat
Half the load and twice the dogs
Hire an experienced driver to lead the team for them
Leave Mercedes behind in town
questions.evidence: Half the load and twice the dogs

questions.q: "And so it went, the inexorable elimination of the superfluous." What does "superfluous" mean here?
choices: Things that were too heavy to lift by hand
Things that were extra and not needed
Things that were broken beyond repair
Things that belonged to other travellers
questions.evidence: the inexorable elimination of the superfluous

questions.q: Why was it a mistake for Charles and Hal to use fourteen dogs on one sled?
choices: Fourteen dogs would fight too much to be harnessed in a single line
The trail to Dawson was too narrow for such a long team to fit
One sled could not carry enough food for fourteen hungry dogs
The law in Skaguay allowed only twelve dogs to pull each sled
questions.evidence: one sled could not carry the food for fourteen dogs

questions.q: How did Buck feel about his new masters as the days went by?
choices: He grew fond of Mercedes because she sometimes fed him extra fish
He felt that there was no depending on any of the three
He respected Hal because he drove the team very hard
He trusted Charles, who was the gentlest of the three
questions.evidence: there was no depending upon these two men and the woman

questions.q: What mistake did Hal make with the dog-food early in the trip?
choices: He left half the fish behind in Skaguay to lighten the sled
He doubled the ration, so the food ran out too soon
He traded the fish to a miner for a new revolver
He let the food get wet, so that it spoiled on the trail
questions.evidence: He doubled it.

questions.q: What was the one thing the three travellers were never too tired to do?
choices: Quarrel with one another
Feed and care for the dogs
Write letters to their family
Study the map to find the trail
questions.evidence: To quarrel was the one thing they were never too weary to do.

questions.q: Why did Mercedes's riding on the sled make things so much worse?
choices: She kept changing the directions and confused the dogs on the trail
She added a heavy load to the sled for the weak, starving dogs
She took up the space that had been saved for the food
She frightened the dogs by crying loudly all through the day
questions.evidence: a lusty last straw to the load dragged by the weak and starving animals

questions.q: When the dog-food gave out, what did Hal trade his revolver for?
choices: A sack of dried salmon from a fishing camp
A few pounds of frozen horse-hide
Two fresh dogs from an old woman's village
A lighter sled
questions.evidence: a few pounds of frozen horse-hide for the Colt's revolver

questions.q: Near the end of the trip it was beautiful spring weather. How did the travellers and dogs react to it?
choices: They stopped for a few days to rest and enjoy the warm sunshine
They were too worn out and miserable to even notice it
They hurried faster because the warm weather made them cheerful
They were frightened by the honking geese flying overhead
questions.evidence: neither dogs nor humans were aware of it

questions.q: What did John Thornton warn Hal about at White River?
choices: The rotten ice
A pack of wolves waiting farther down the trail
The angry miners in Dawson who would steal his dogs
A storm coming that would bury the trail in snow
questions.evidence: Thornton's warning to take no more chances on the rotten ice

questions.q: Why did Buck refuse to get up when Hal ordered the team on?
choices: He was waiting for Thornton to give him something to eat first
He sensed that disaster waited on the thin ice ahead
He wanted Sol-leks to take a turn leading the team
He was angry that Hal had sold his old friend Billee
questions.evidence: he sensed disaster close at hand, out there ahead on the ice

questions.q: What happened after John Thornton cut Buck's traces and the others went on without him?
choices: They reached Dawson safely and sold the rest of the team
They turned back to Skaguay because the ice was too thin
The ice broke and the sled, dogs and people disappeared
They camped a mile away and came back the next morning
questions.evidence: The bottom had dropped out of the trail.
